intro: To change the page orientation to landscape in Word on Mac, navigate to the Layout tab and select Orientation. You can then choose Landscape to update your entire document or specific sections as needed.

blocks.text: Changing page orientation for the entire document

Most users want to switch their entire document to landscape mode to accommodate wide tables or images. This is the simplest task in Word for Mac. Open your document and look at the ribbon at the top of the window. Click the Layout tab. You will see an icon labeled Orientation. Click it and select Landscape. Your document will instantly update. Every page will rotate to the horizontal layout.
How to change orientation for specific pages

Sometimes you need one page in landscape while the rest stay in portrait. Word handles this through section breaks. You must isolate the page you want to change. Place your cursor at the very start of the content that needs a new orientation. Navigate to Layout and click Breaks. Select Next Page. Now repeat this at the end of that specific content block. This creates a distinct section for your landscape page.

Once the section exists, click anywhere inside it. Go back to the Layout tab. Instead of just clicking the Orientation button, click the small arrow icon in the corner of the Page Setup group. This opens the full Page Setup dialog. Choose Landscape. In the Apply to dropdown menu, ensure you select This section. Click OK. Only your chosen pages will rotate.
Word for the web versus desktop app

Many users try to change orientation in the web browser version of Word. The web version is built for basic editing. It lacks the advanced page layout controls found in the desktop app. If you do not see the full Page Setup dialog, you are likely in the web view. Click the Open in Word button in your browser to launch the desktop app. You will then have access to all formatting tools.

items: The whole document changes: You likely skipped the section breaks. Ensure you have a Next Page break before and after the content.
Orientation reverts: Check your Normal.dotm template. It might contain old settings. You can rename the file to force Word to create a fresh one.
Printing errors: If the document looks right on screen but prints wrong, check the File > Print menu. Verify that the printer settings match your landscape layout.
Grayed out options: If you cannot click layout features, check your document permissions or ensure the file is not in Read Only mode.

blocks.text: Why formatting matters in your workflow

Formatting tasks often interrupt your flow. With frequent distractions, finding the right menu quickly is helpful. Word is a deep application. Learning where the layout tools live saves time. Whether you are building a report or a simple letter, knowing these steps makes your work easier.
Keeping your Mac Word version current

Microsoft updates Word for Mac regularly. If you experience strange behavior, like settings not saving, check your update status. Go to Help in the menu bar and click Check for Updates. Keeping your software on the latest version ensures you have the correct menu paths. As of October 2026, the current version is 16.114.1. Always ensure your macOS is also up to date to maintain stability.

faq.question: Why can I not change orientation in Word for the web?
faq.answer: Word for the web is designed for light editing and lacks advanced layout features like section-specific orientation. You must use the desktop version for these tasks.

faq.question: How do I print only one landscape page?
faq.answer: If you have set up your document with section breaks, you can print the specific page by going to File > Print and entering the page number in the range field.

faq.question: Does changing orientation affect my headers and footers?
faq.answer: Yes, changing orientation can sometimes cause headers and footers to shift. You may need to adjust their margins in the Page Setup dialog after changing the page layout.
